findings.title: Join timeout exits loop before terminating flusher processes
findings.body: In `SpanFlusher.join`, when the deadline expires the loop breaks before reaching `process.terminate()` at line 346. Since `next_step.join(timeout)` is called first and can consume the whole timeout, this can leave all spawned flusher processes alive after a rebalance or shutdown. Those daemon processes keep flushing and producing from their old shard assignments, and a new flusher for the same shards may then produce duplicate segments and leak processes. Remaining processes must be terminated even when the wait deadline is exceeded.

findings.title: Invalid flusher process count can disable flushing entirely
findings.body: `--flusher-processes` is an unvalidated integer. If a negative value is supplied, `self.max_processes = max_processes or ...` keeps it and `num_processes = min(...)` becomes negative. `range(self.num_processes)` is then empty, so no flusher processes or per-process buffers are created; spans are written to Redis but never flushed. A value of 0 is also silently treated as "all shards" rather than rejected. The process count should be validated to be at least 1.

findings.title: New multiprocess flusher path is not exercised by tests
findings.body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` passes `produce_to_pipe`, which makes `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards` use the `threading.Thread` branch instead of `mp_context.Process`. The assertions therefore only verify shard-to-thread mapping; they never exercise spawning real child processes, the per-process `SpansBuffer` in a child, process death/restart detection, or shutdown of `multiprocessing.Process` objects. Since the core change is the multiprocess flusher, regressions in the actual production path would not be caught.

findings.title: Added synchronization sleep is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: The test replaces `time.sleep` with `lambda _: None` at line 15, so the new `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62 does not actually wait despite the comment saying it gives flusher threads time to process after the drift change. The test relies on incidental thread scheduling and can be flaky; use the original sleep function or an explicit synchronization primitive instead.

findings.title: wait_produce metric uses inconsistent shard tag key
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and the unhealthy metric use the tag key `shard`, but `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` at line 199 uses `shards`. Dashboards or alerts filtering by the `shard` tag will not include producer wait time, so this metric becomes effectively invisible in existing shard-level queries.

findings.title: Docstring incorrectly says one process per shard
findings.body: The class docstring says the flusher "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing," but `max_processes` caps the number of processes and the CLI default is 1, so multiple shards can be handled by a single process. The documentation should describe the capped/process-sharing behavior to avoid misleading operators about resource usage and concurrency.
